title: Contributor Growth & Perks Playbook
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Summary

This playbook summarizes the expected outcomes at each contributor level (IC and Manager tracks), links levels to the primary benefits and allowances, and provides a compact hiring and onboarding checklist keyed to level. It is intended for hiring managers, ICs planning moves, and people-ops partners executing offers.

How to use this doc
- Managers: use snapshots to set 30/60/90 goals and to calibrate offers.
- People Ops: map benefits in offers using the benefits table.
- ICs: reference signals of success to prepare promotion packets.

Contributor level snapshots (condensed)
- IC1: Focus on learning systems, completing well-scoped tasks, and driving small fixes. Key signals: reliable PRs, test coverage contributions, active participation in code reviews. Typical tenure: 0-18 months.

- IC2: Own small features end-to-end, reduce support work, and collaborate with product. Key signals: feature ownership, measurable user impact, cross-team communication. Typical tenure: 12-30 months.

- IC3: Lead designs for medium-scope services, mentor junior ICs, and own operational metrics for areas. Key signals: architecture proposals adopted, mentoring records, measurable improvements (latency/cost/availability). Typical tenure: 24-48 months.

- IC4: Drive cross-team technical initiatives, publish internal standards, and influence product strategy. Key signals: multi-team project leadership, new platform capabilities delivered, recognized subject-matter expertise. Typical tenure: 36+ months.

- IC5: Company-level technical leadership, long-term strategy, and external representation. Key signals: technical strategy outcomes, major platform wins, external talks/publications encouraged. Typical tenure: exceptional / long-tenured.

Manager track (condensed)
- Mgr1: First-line people manager for a single team. Responsibilities: hiring, performance coaching, delivery oversight.
- Mgr2: Manager of managers or large functional area, accountable for multiple product deliveries and retention.
- Mgr3: Director-level leadership aligned with product and business goals, owning hiring strategy and org-level outcomes.

Benefits & perks mapping (high-level rules)
- Health coverage: medical/dental/vision are available from day one to all employees.
- Paid time off: baseline 20 days for entry levels; increases at mid-senior tiers and via tenure reviews.
- L&D: annual learning stipend scales by level (entry: $1,200; senior and managers: $2,500). Conference budgets are approval-based and increase for senior contributors.
- Home office & ergonomics: onboarding stipend for all; recurring ergonomic allowance for mid-senior contributors.
- Equipment upgrades: standard laptop + monitor on day one; eligibility for accelerated refresh at senior levels.
- Equity & bonus: equity offered based on level and role; variable bonuses begin at mid-contributor and manager tiers.
- Mental health & coaching: EAP for everyone; expanded coaching allowance for senior contributors and managers.

Hiring & offer checklist (level-aware)
1) Role brief (Hiring manager): include level, 3 success signals, expected first 90-day plan, and interview rubric. Target slot fill duration: 6-10 weeks for IC1-IC2, 8-16 weeks for senior hires.

2) Interview loop & scoring (Hiring team): use standardized scorecard; include at least one cross-functional interviewer and one domain expert. Document calibration notes on final decision.

3) Offer packaging (People Ops): map benefits to level using the playbook. If additional perks are requested (accelerated L&D, special hardware), include manager justification.

4) Preboarding (People Ops): send welcome materials, first-week agenda, assigned buddy, and mentor pairing 3-5 business days before start. Create IT ticket bundle for provisioning.

5) Day 0-7 (Manager + IT): confirm laptop and SSO, add to team channels, schedule Day 1 orientation and role expectation meeting, and set first-week small delivery (doc or README).

6) Week 2-12 ramp (Manager): document 30/60/90 goals in HR system, weekly check-ins for the first month, shadow rotations for on-call roles, and required compliance training completion by week 4.

Tool access quick matrix
- SSO/Identity: People Ops initiates; Security approves elevated access.
- GitHub: repo owners approve based on team list.
- Cloud consoles: infra owner grants least-privilege roles.
- Observability (Datadog/BigQuery dashboards): product or infra owners grant viewer/editor roles.
- ML resources (GPU reservations): ML infra team approves requests; project justification required.

Promotion & mobility: process summary
- Packet submission: manager or IC submits a short packet including outcomes, artifacts, and peer feedback.
- Calibration panel: includes a senior manager, HR partner, and cross-functional peers.
- Outcome & comp: HR records level changes; compensation changes processed via comp committee when needed.
- Backfill: hiring manager opens requisition; internal mobility pipeline available for fast reallocation.

Manager expectations (first 90 days)
- Provide a 30/60/90 plan, assign a peer buddy, create clear onboarding goals in the HR system, and schedule performance calibration at 90 days.

Operational targets for the playbook
- First-week provisioning success rate target: >95% (measured by IT ticket resolution within 72 hours).
- Promotion packet completeness: checklist compliance target >90%.
- Internal mobility fill time for IC1-IC2: median <6 weeks.

Templates & supporting links
- Role brief template: see related pages.
- Interview scorecard and loop templates: see related pages.
- Promotion packet template: search in the roles-and-career space.

Change log

Owner & governance

- Review cadence: annual or after material changes to benefits or hiring processes.

End of document
